content: To better understand the contribution of each component, we perform an ablation study on subword-level experiments. The results are shown in Table TABREF37. In `-MT noise' setting, we do not add noise to source sentences for MT. In `-weight sharing' setting, we use different parameters in CTC classification layer and source embedding layer. These two experiments prove that both weight sharing and using noisy MT input benefit to the final translation quality. Performance degrades more in `-weight sharing', indicating the semantic consistency contributes more to our model. In the `-pretrain' experiment, we remove the pre-training stage and directly update the model on three tasks, leading to a dramatic decrease on BLEU score, indicating the pre-training is an indispensable step for end-to-end ST.
